layers.name: Runtime Bootstrap And Core
layers.description: Bootstrap, Lua/runtime services, shared utilities, and the core conversation engine that keep the Dialogue System running in play mode.

layers.name: Conversation Runtime
layers.description: MVC flow, sequencing, and conversation data-processing code that advances dialogue state and branching.

layers.name: UI And Scene Integration
layers.description: Runtime UI, actor adapters, and trigger-driven scene integration used to surface conversations to players and NPCs.

layers.name: State And Persistence
layers.description: Quest state, saved variables, and persistence bridges that preserve dialogue progress and gameplay-facing state.

layers.name: Authoring And Tooling
layers.description: Unity Editor windows, custom inspectors, import pipelines, and configuration helpers used while authoring dialogue content.

layers.name: Wrappers And Extension Points
layers.description: Third-party wrappers plus template scripts that show the vendor-supported customization path without forking core code.

tour.title: Start With Runtime Bootstrap
tour.description: Begin with the scene-level manager and bootstrap path. These files establish the singleton controller, database loading, and the entry path most gameplay code touches first.

tour.title: Follow The Conversation Pipeline
tour.description: Trace the main MVC runtime next. These files show how authored entries become evaluated conversation state, then routed to the active view and sequencer.

tour.title: Inspect Player-Facing UI And Triggers
tour.description: These files are the main scene-composition surfaces for projects integrating Dialogue System into actual gameplay and menu flows.

tour.title: Check Lua, Quest, And Save State
tour.description: When a task involves variables, quest state, save-load, or runtime database mutation, these files define the supported implementation path.

tour.title: Use Supported Extension Points
tour.description: Before modifying plugin internals, review the wrappers and template scripts that encode the vendor-supported customization path.
